bullets.title: June NFP Due Today: Market Pricing ~115-133k, Below Survey; Fed Hike Odds in Focus
bullets.body: Consensus expects ~110-115k June nonfarm payrolls; surveyed traders forecast 133k with 4.2% unemployment (vs 4.3% consensus) and 0.3% AHE. 22V Research argues a September hike (currently at 73% market odds) is unlikely if Core PCE stays at 0.21% MoM, while GS notes the market is only pricing ~30% odds of a July move. In-line or weaker payrolls are viewed as bullish for yields; declining unemployment would be hawkish by increasing odds of sticky core services inflation.

bullets.title: AI Infrastructure Selloff: META Cloud Announcement Torches Neocloud Stocks -12-17%
bullets.body: META announced plans to sell excess AI compute capacity (Meta Compute) via both hosted API/model-access and raw GPU capacity models, sending shares +9% on improved ROIC perception but cratering CRWV -14% and NBIS -17% as META becomes a direct neocloud competitor. JPM estimates 1 GW of META capacity could generate ~$20B annual revenue and several dollars of EPS; MS calculates every 250 MW leased at $40/W adds ~$3 (8%) to 2028 EPS. Multiple analysts frame this as optionality/Plan B while 2027 META capex estimates range from $175B-$275B vs Street consensus $160B.

bullets.title: Asian Tech Rout: Korea -8%, Kospi Circuit Breaker; AI Capacity Concerns Drive 2-Sigma Moves
bullets.body: Korea's Kospi fell >8% overnight — triggering a futures trading halt — with SK Hynix and Samsung (>50% of index) collapsing 18% and 15% respectively on Apple's reported talks to source memory from sanctioned Chinese suppliers CXMT and YMTC. GS TMT Momentum Pair finished -9.62% (second drawdown in a week); Japan fell -2.5%, China -2%. Roth notes Asian tech underperformance was approximately two standard deviations in the CSI 300 and Kospi.

bullets.title: Apple Pursuing Sanctioned Chinese Memory Chips (CXMT, YMTC) Amid DRAM Supply Crunch
bullets.body: Apple is in active negotiations to source DRAM from ChangXin Memory (CXMT) and NAND from Yangtze Memory (YMTC) — both on the Pentagon's 1260H blacklist — to address an unprecedented memory supply crunch as suppliers shift capacity to HBM for AI data centers. Apple is lobbying Washington for political cover; the move signals AI infrastructure demand is crowding out consumer electronics memory supply. PC DDR4 spot prices hit $21 in June (+5% MoM, +7x YoY); commodity NAND reached $28.8 (+8.7% MoM, 18th consecutive monthly gain).

bullets.title: Memory Price Supercycle: DRAM +7x YoY, NAND +9x YoY; Supply Crunch to Last Past 2027
bullets.body: PC DRAM ASPs rose 23-25% MoM in April-May; TrendForce raised 3Q DRAM forecast to 15-20% QoQ growth (from 8-13%). Samsung HBM4E yield exceeded 70%, entering stable production for NVIDIA Vera Rubin Ultra. Micron CEO confirmed the supply crunch persists beyond 2027, partly caused by customer pricing pressure in prior years suppressing capex; Micron is investing ~$200B in new fabs. SK Hynix ($64.4B) and Samsung ($90B) both announced massive domestic Korean semiconductor capex commitments.

bullets.title: NVIDIA Launches Revenue-Sharing Model with AI Cloud Partners; Adds Recurring Usage-Linked Income
bullets.body: NVIDIA introduced a new business model where AI cloud partners deploy Grace Blackwell GPUs and NVIDIA earns standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenues. Firmus is building a 360 MW DSX AI factory in Indonesia with up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs; Sharon AI deploying up to 40,000 GB300 GPUs. JPM's industry model projects AI DC switch market surging +116% YoY in 2026 to $24B (+40% CAGR through 2030), with NVDA at 50% AI DC switch share.

bullets.title: AI Infrastructure TAM Revisions Up Sharply: Server Market +67% YoY to $473B in 2026
bullets.body: JPM raised AI infrastructure TAM forecasts materially: total server market +67% YoY to $473B in 2026 with +31% CAGR through 2030; AI server segment at +37% CAGR. Data center Ethernet switch market reaches $46B (+43% YoY). AEC market exploding +121% YoY. DELL server share jumped to 21% from 10% a year ago; ANET holds 22% of total DC Ethernet. DCI market revised +22% for 2027 and +28% for 2028 vs prior March outlook.

bullets.title: SaaS Multiples Compressed; IGV -16.5% YTD vs S&P +7.5%; Software vs Semis Ratio Bouncing
bullets.body: Wolfe's All-SaaS index trades at 4.9x FY+2 EV/Sales; IGV has returned -16.5% YTD vs S&P 500 +7.5%. GS notes the Software vs. Semis ratio bounced 9% Wednesday (up from -59% YTD) as rotation pressure on semiconductor momentum builds. Skew normalization in AI-exposed indices reinforces the consolidation view; hedge funds sold NDX while buying SPX/RTY futures.

bullets.title: Tariff Regime Becoming Durable: Section 301/232 Converges to ~9-10% Statutory Rate
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flags tariff structure shifting from temporary IEEPA emergency measures to a more rules-based Section 301/232 framework. Section 122 tariffs expire July 24; July 7 Section 301 hearings are the next procedural catalyst. Statutory effective rate estimated at 9-10% with less dispersion than the original regime; lower uncertainty should support capex at the margin but broad reshoring evidence remains limited. Pharma tariffs modeled at 15%.

bullets.title: FOMC Dot Plot Hawkish; Gold -11.7%, Silver -21.6% in June; EM Equities -1.7% MoM Despite +23% Q2
bullets.body: June FOMC was unexpectedly hawkish with nine dot-plot members anticipating hikes this year, six looking for two or more moves. MSCI EM +23.3% for Q2 2026 (best quarter since 2Q09) but gave back -1.7% in June on Fed hawkishness and strong dollar (DXY +2.3%). Precious metals crashed — Gold -11.7%, Silver -21.6% — while industrial metals (Aluminium -17.3%, Copper -3.1%) also sold off. Warsh remarks are seen as supporting a debasement trade (long gold, short dollar, steeper curve).

bullets.title: Oil Down 3rd Straight Session; Hormuz Reopening Drives Supply Glut; UBS Cuts Brent to $84
bullets.body: WTI crude fell ~1.94% pre-market to $67.25; oil has declined three consecutive sessions following the Iran-US MoU extending ceasefire 60 days and reopening the Strait of Hormuz. UAE exports recovered to pre-war levels of 3.9M bpd. Brent and WTI fell >20% in June. UBS cut its 2026 Brent forecast to $84/bbl from $93 on the faster-than-expected Hormuz recovery.

bullets.title: Russell 2000 Outperforms S&P by 12pp YTD; Post-Rebalance AI Exposure Cut from 15% to 7%
bullets.body: The Russell 2000 outperformed the S&P 500 by 12 percentage points YTD, with ~40% of that driven by AI infrastructure stocks and ~10% contributed by biotech (11% of index weight). The Russell rebalance materially reduced AI infrastructure exposure from 15% to 7% of the index. Pre-payroll positioning survey shows highest risk-on sentiment since December 2025, with 52% expecting a risk-on market reaction.

bullets.title: GOOGL Loses €4.13B EU Android Antitrust Appeal; Court Found Intentional Infringement
bullets.body: The European Court of Justice upheld the full €4.13B ($4.70B) fine against Google for requiring Android manufacturers to preinstall Google Search and Chrome, dismissing the appeal and finding the infringement was intentional. GOOGL fell ~1% in pre-market. The fine was originally €4.34B before being reduced in 2022.

bullets.title: Hedgehog Bearish Signal: KOSPI Breaks Trade Support; QQQ Vol at -8% Discount to 30-Day Realized
bullets.body: McCullough (Hedgeye) flags KOSPI broke TRADE Signal Support at 8296, calling it a 'bubble pop starting parts 1-2 of 3.' QQQ implied volatility is at an -8% discount to 30-day realized vol, a sharp reversal from a +60% premium one month ago, suggesting consensus is crowded long large-cap tech/semis. CPI Nowcast for July at 3.59% (down from 4.25% cycle peak) pointing to Quad 4 disinflation dynamics.

bullets.title: Retail Investor Dip-Buying Semis at 14-Month High Inflows; Futures Traders Net Sold $11.3B
bullets.body: JPM retail radar shows semis inflows at highest levels in 14+ months: MU topped purchases at $897M (+3.7z) and SNDK at $705M (+4.6z) following blockbuster MU earnings. NVDA accumulated $492M in retail purchases. However, futures traders net sold ~$11.3B (ES -$7.3B, NQ -$2.2B, RTY -$1.8B), while AAII bull-bear spread sits at -10.9% despite BofA Street equity allocation at 56.2%.

bullets.title: June US Auto SAAR 16.5M Beats; BEV Penetration Falls to 5.3% from 7.9% a Year Ago
bullets.body: June US light vehicle SAAR hit 16.5M, beating JPM's 16.2M estimate and Bloomberg consensus 16.1M, boosted by fleet/truck demand. Tesla came in at ~37K units (-27% YoY); BEV penetration dropped to 5.3% from 7.9% in June 2025. Hybrid share rose to 16.1% YoY. Franchise dealers are most favorably positioned given brand-mix tailwinds.

bullets.title: German Reform Package: 33 Proposals Including €10B Tax Cuts, Labor Flexibility, and AI/Grid Policy
bullets.body: Germany's coalition government announced 33 reform proposals spanning tax (€10B in cuts for low/middle incomes, ~0.2% of GDP), labor market flexibility (expanded fixed-term contracts, tighter sick-leave, easier high-income layoffs), and industrial policy (autonomous driving support, faster grid/planning approvals). One-third of measures target cutting red tape to EU minimum levels. Government committed to converting all 33 proposals into law by end of 2026; industry groups are supportive, opposition parties critical.

bullets.title: Pre-Market Snapshot: S&P Futures Flat, NDX -0.4%; Semis/Cloud Resilient, RBLX -4.2%
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures up 0.06% at 7,548; 10-year Treasury yield +2 bps to 4.50%; WTI -1.94% to $67.25. Pre-market leaders include PLTR +2.4% (DA Davidson upgrade to Buy), ADBE +1.9% (HSBC upgrade to Buy, $308 PT), INTC +1.8%, and defense names AVAV +5.5%/KTOS +3.0%. Laggards include RBLX -4.2%, RDDT -1.2%, OMC -4.9%. European indices up 0.5-0.9%.

bullets.title: Q2 Earnings Season Kickoff July 13; Street Expects ~23% S&P EPS Growth; Semis ~Half of Total
bullets.body: Q2 earnings season begins the week of July 13 with Street consensus at ~23% S&P 500 earnings growth. Semiconductor companies are expected to account for nearly half of total S&P 500 earnings growth. Healthcare is expected to outperform in 3Q on midterm election seasonality; biotech historically strongest in 3Q midterm years (+11%).

bullets.title: Chinese Brands Hit 12.5% W. Europe Auto Share in May (+4.6pp YoY); German OEMs Lose Most Share
bullets.body: Chinese auto brands reached 12.5% of Western Europe passenger vehicle market share in May 2026 (+4.6pp YoY), with sales +62.4% YoY to 128K units vs. sector +3.3%. BYD leads Chinese NEV brands at 24.0% W. Europe NEV share (+7.3pp YoY); German brands lost 3.1pp of share and European NEV share fell 8.1pp. US brands gained 1.6pp largely on Tesla growth. EV penetration in the region hit 36.4% (+7.4pp YoY).
